title: Candidate Momentum Dashboard & Rapid Onboard Kit
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact operational playbook + lightweight dashboard template to keep candidate momentum high and reduce time-to-offer for engineering IC roles. It pairs (A) SLA targets and trigger signals, (B) a single-page evidence-capture rubric for interviewers, and (C) a 30-day rapid-onboard checklist to get new hires productive in the first month.

Notes on usage (quick):
- Primary users: recruiters, hiring managers, interviewers, onboarding buddy.
- Single source to paste into a candidate Git doc or ATS quick note.
- Use the SLA targets below as goals; escalate misses to talent-ops channel #hiring-triage.

Part A — Momentum SLA targets and trigger signals:
- Screen scheduling target: within 48h of resume pass (owner: recruiter).
- Full loop (phone+tech+onsite) target: 10 business days from screen.
- Offer decision target: 2 business days after final on-site.
- Candidate follow-up cadence: recruiter updates candidate at least every 72h when loop is active.
- Fast-track triggers (immediate escalation and can do same-week loop):
  * Referral from engineering director OR current headcount-critical tag.
  * Candidate already has signed offer window <7 days with another employer.
  * Hiring manager consensus that candidate clears bar on first take (document in the note).
- Hold signals (slow loop):
  * Needs relocation beyond policy scope, non-starter for immediate schedule.
  * Candidate unavailable >14 days for interviews.

Part B — One-page interviewer evidence capture (paste into candidate shared note):
Header: role / level / interviewer / date / stage (phone/tech/design)
Scoring (0–4): examples and guidance below. Add 1–3 bullet evidence points and a pass/review flag.
- Technical correctness (0 none / 1 poor / 2 mixed / 3 solid / 4 exceptional): examples of correctness, edge-case handling.
- System design (0 none / 1 naive / 2 ok components / 3 clear tradeoffs / 4 system-level thinking): list diagrams or tradeoffs they raised.
- Problem-solving & debugging (0 can't iterate / 1 stumbles / 2 gets to working idea / 3 iterates well / 4 elegant heuristics + tests): note approach to failing cases.
- Collaboration & clarity (0 unclear / 1 terse / 2 reasonable / 3 good communicator / 4 leader): mention how they handled hints and partnered with you.
- Product sense (0 none / 1 surface / 2 feature-aware / 3 strong tradeoffs / 4 drives product decisions): when applicable.
- Overall hire recommendation: Strong/Neutral/No. Quick sentence rationale (1 line).

Example evidence capture (copyable):
- Interviewer: Priya Nair — 2025-06-12 — Tech phone
  * Technical correctness: 3 — solved primary algorithm, identified O(N log N) improvement, caught edge case for empty input.
  * System design: 2 — proposed cache + DB, missing eviction policy discussion.
  * Collaboration: 4 — asked clarifying Qs, aligned on constraints quickly.
  * Recommendation: Strong — appropriate for L3 backend IC, recommends paired design follow-up.

Scoring guidance (quick cheatsheet for interviewers):
- 4 (Exceptional): demonstrates depth, mentors during interview, adds measurable improvements, supports tradeoffs.
- 3 (Strong): meets bar, good judgment, few omissions.
- 2 (Borderline): implementable but needs coaching; acceptable for some levels with evidence.
- 1 (Below bar): significant omissions or incorrect assumptions.
- 0 (No signal): insufficient evidence to score.

Part C — Rapid 0–30 day onboard kit (concise checklist for hiring manager + buddy):
Day 0 (acceptance -> first day):
- Hiring manager: send welcome note with 90-day impact canvas + 1st-week goals (owner: HM).
- IT/Security: confirm laptop, KMS access, and invite to security orientation (owner: infra ops).
- Buddy: schedule 1:1 for first-day 30-minute orientation and calendar shares.
- People Ops: finalize paperwork, benefits orientation slot.

Week 1 (days 1–7):
- Day 1: 30/60/90 shipped doc + team tour (ownership: HM/buddy).
- Day 2–3: engineering environment bootstraps (repo access, ci pipelines, local run). "Quick run" task: get a local smoke test passing (owner: eng onboarding lead).
- End of week: 1:1 with HM to set milestones + quick wins list.

Week 2 (days 8–14):
- Shadow rotation: pair with 2 team members for small debugging tasks (owner: buddy).
- First small PR: aim to author or meaningfully update a PR.
- Check: security checklist reviewed and completed.

Weeks 3–4 (days 15–30):
- Deliverable: complete a scoped ticket that touches infra and app area by day 30.
- Feedback loop: 30-day retro with HM and hiring manager; log signals: blockers, tooling gaps.

Onboarding signals (to watch):
- Red: no access to repo or CI by day 3 / cannot run test suite by day 7.
- Yellow: PR not merged after 7 days despite active ownership.
- Green: PR merged and first bug fix shipped within 30 days.

Communication templates (snippets you can copy):
- Recruiter -> candidate after screen (48h): "Thanks again for the call — next steps: we aim to schedule a technical interview within 10 business days. I'll keep you posted; if timing becomes tight on your side, please flag ASAP. — <recruiter>"
- Manager -> new hire on day 1: "Welcome! My ask for week 1: get your dev environment green and ship a README improvement PR. I'll check in end of week."

Open questions / TODOs (quick backlog):
- Add JIT interview compensation guidance for competitive counter-offers (owner: compops).
- Connect this doc to ATS webhooks to auto-update candidate momentum dashboard (owner: eng-recruiting).
- Run a 60-day pilot with two teams to validate SLA targets and adjust fast-track heuristics.

Searchable keywords for ATS and folders: candidate-momentum, fast-track-hire, 30-day-rapid-onboard, evidence-capture, interview-onepage.

Slack channels & contacts (for escalation):
- #hiring-triage (primary) — escalate if SLA missed >48h.
- #people-ops (secondary) — benefits or paperwork block.
- On-call recruiting: Maya Chen (mchen@redwood.ai) / Liam Ortiz (lortiz@redwood.ai).
